subject: radiology
title: Angioplasty and stents

steps.tx: Arterial opening starts with a balloon, and a stent follows only when the balloon result stays unsafe. **Balloon angioplasty** cracks plaque and stretches the vessel media during controlled inflation inside the narrowed segment. The operator reserves **provisional stenting** for a flow limiting dissection or for elastic recoil after deflation. A **self expanding stent** suits the mobile femoropopliteal segment, while a balloon expandable stent gives precision at an ostium. Iliac disease stents readily, whereas long femoropopliteal disease often starts with a drug coated balloon alone.
steps.say: Arterial opening starts with a balloon and a stent follows only when the balloon result stays unsafe. The balloon cracks plaque and stretches the vessel wall during controlled inflation inside the narrowing. The operator reserves a stent for a flow limiting dissection or for recoil after deflation. A flexible stent suits the mobile thigh segment while a balloon expanded stent gives ostial precision. Iliac disease stents readily whereas long thigh disease often starts with a drug coated balloon.

steps.tx: Drug delivery changed arterial patency because the wall receives antiproliferative treatment during a brief contact. A **drug coated balloon** lines the wall with paclitaxel and leaves no metal behind after treatment ends. That approach suits **in stent restenosis** and small vessels where another metal layer would crowd the lumen. A **drug eluting stent** adds a scaffold when recoil threatens the result after balloon inflation alone. Recurrence presents with claudication and a rising duplex velocity, and coated angioplasty inside the old stent treats that recurrence.

steps.tx: Carotid and renal stenting stay selective, and the examiner rewards a student who knows when not to stent. **Carotid artery stenting** suits a symptomatic patient who carries **high surgical risk** for endarterectomy under anaesthesia. An **embolic protection device** catches debris during deployment and that capture lowers stroke risk during the case. Routine renal stenting for hypertension lost favour because large trials showed no added benefit over medical therapy. Renal **fibromuscular dysplasia** still responds to plain angioplasty, and subclavian steal also stents well in selected patients.
steps.say: Carotid and renal stenting stay selective and a good answer knows when not to stent. Carotid stenting suits a symptomatic patient who carries high surgical risk for open surgery. A protection device catches debris during deployment and that capture lowers stroke risk during the case. Routine renal stenting lost favour because large trials showed no added benefit over medicines. Renal dysplasia is still responsive to plain balloon treatment and subclavian steal also stents well.

steps.tx: This lateral carotid angiogram shows a tight stenosis at the origin of the internal carotid artery with a stent across the lesion. The labels compare the narrow segment with the normal distal vessel for a **NASCET measurement** of stenosis severity. A filter type **embolic protection device** sits beyond the lesion and catches debris while the operator deploys the stent. The image matters for the exam because carotid stenting suits a symptomatic patient with high surgical risk. Protection and careful measurement together decide whether stenting beats surgery for that patient.

steps.tx: Durability after angioplasty rests on symptoms and surveillance together, never on the final angiogram alone. A better **ankle brachial index** with returning pulses marks technical success while the patient remains on the table. **Duplex surveillance** with velocity ratios watches for restenosis before symptoms return to the leg again. Claudication should improve clearly before the team counts the result as clinical success for that patient. A limb with tissue loss needs **straight line flow** to the foot, often through below knee angioplasty, before healing follows.
steps.say: Durability after angioplasty rests on symptoms and surveillance together never on the final picture alone. A better pressure index with returning pulses marks technical success while the patient stays on the table. Duplex surveillance with velocity ratios watches for narrowing before symptoms return to the leg. Leg pain should improve clearly before the team counts the result as clinical success. A limb with tissue loss needs direct flow to the foot before healing follows properly.
